maya: new contributor report — Ruby SDK auth retries failing on Windows 10. Token refresh succeeds but subsequent retry gets 400 due to header being truncated.
oliver: can you paste the raw request headers? sometimes powershell env var expands weirdly
maya: pasted snippet:
```
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_very_long_token_part_that_gets_truncated...
Content-Type: application/json
```
kevin: hmm, truncation looks like CRLF vs LF handling in HTTP client when using Net::HTTP on certain Windows Ruby builds
jen: is this reproducible in CI? we don't run Windows in sampleapp matrix regularly
maya: I repro locally on Windows + Ruby 3.1. The cause seems to be an old dependency `httpclient` that calls `strip` differently on `
` and ends up chopping headers over a certain length
oliver: can you try forcing the default `net/http` path or upgrading `httpclient`?
maya: tried pinning `httpclient` to 2.8.3 and it fixed the truncation. Opened PR to bump and add a regression test that asserts header pass-through for long tokens: https://git.example.com/redwood/rb-sdk/pulls/314
devex-bot: PR 314 opened by maya in rb-sdk — reviewers requested: kevin, jen
kevin: nice minimal fix. Add a Windows CI job in rb-sdk to catch regressions. Also add a one-liner in the sampleapp quickstart about Windows dev prerequisites and testing.
jen: tiny nit — add a test that simulates CRLF header serialization to avoid future surprises
maya: added test + Windows job in CI matrix on the branch, PR updated
oliver: review done, LGTM after small test tweak
kevin: merging after CI
maya: merged, will follow up with a short note in devex about potential Windows quirks and how to reproduce locally (powershell example). Filed doc issue: https://git.example.com/redwood/devex/issues/620
maya: thanks all :heart:
